# Semantic categories

What RobustEHR can target and what it reports hits against. Every
category is a set of UMLS semantic types, so membership is a lookup
against a published terminology rather than a judgement call.

<!-- Generated by validation/pipeline/scripts/gen_category_docs.py from
     src/robustehr/resources/semantic_categories.yaml. Do not edit by hand. -->

## Hierarchy

```
anatomy
device
disorder
├── disease
├── symptom
└── finding   (excluded from clinical_any)
lab_measurement
lab_result
medication
procedure
├── therapeutic_procedure
└── diagnostic_procedure
```

## Categories

### `anatomy` — Anatomy

Body parts, regions, spaces, tissues and substances. Carries the site and laterality information that a diagnosis is anchored to, so corrupting it changes where a finding is located without changing what it is.

| Category | Tier | Definition | Semantic types |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anatomy` | `anchored` | _(above)_ | T017 Anatomical Structure, T018 Embryonic Structure, T021 Fully Formed Anatomical Structure, T022 Body System, T023 Body Part, Organ, or Organ Component, T024 Tissue, T025 Cell, T026 Cell Component, T029 Body Location or Region, T030 Body Space or Junction, T031 Body Substance |

**Validated against:** **SNOMED CT Entity Linking Challenge** → `body structure`

Sheet: [`anatomy_NER_validation.md`](../validation/pipeline/categories/anatomy_NER_validation.md)

### `device` — Medical devices

Instruments, implants and delivery apparatus — catheters, tubes, valves, lines, pumps. Frequently the evidence for a procedure or an ongoing therapy, and often the only mention of either.

| Category | Tier | Definition | Semantic types |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | `unanchored` | _(above)_ | T074 Medical Device, T075 Research Device, T203 Drug Delivery Device |

**Validated against:** _no gold standard covers this._

Sheet: [`device_NER_validation.md`](../validation/pipeline/categories/device_NER_validation.md)

### `disorder` — Disorders

Anything wrong with the patient: diagnoses, syndromes, injuries, and the signs and symptoms that evidence them. The parent every gold standard actually adjudicates, which is why validation happens here and its three children are treated as refinements of a validated boundary.

| Category | Tier | Definition | Semantic types |
|---|---|---|---|
| `disorder` | `anchored` | _(above)_ | T019 Congenital Abnormality, T020 Acquired Abnormality, T033 Finding, T037 Injury or Poisoning, T046 Pathologic Function, T047 Disease or Syndrome, T048 Mental or Behavioral Dysfunction, T049 Cell or Molecular Dysfunction, T050 Experimental Model of Disease, T184 Sign or Symptom, T191 Neoplastic Process |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;↳ `disease` | `derived` | Named pathology — diagnoses, syndromes, neoplasms, injuries and pathologic processes. What a phenotype definition is usually written in terms of. Separated from `symptom` because "the model missed the diagnosis" and "the model missed the symptom" are different failures. | T019 Congenital Abnormality, T020 Acquired Abnormality, T037 Injury or Poisoning, T046 Pathologic Function, T047 Disease or Syndrome, T048 Mental or Behavioral Dysfunction, T049 Cell or Molecular Dysfunction, T050 Experimental Model of Disease, T191 Neoplastic Process |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;↳ `symptom` | `derived` | What the patient reports or the clinician observes, as distinct from the diagnosis it supports — dyspnea, fever, nausea. T184 only; adding T033 Finding would triple the category and fill it with `one` and `normal`. | T184 Sign or Symptom |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;↳ `finding` | `derived` | The broad residual of the disorder hierarchy: clinical observations that are neither a named disease nor a specific symptom. Legitimate at span level ("difficulty climbing stairs") but the noisiest type at word level, which is why it is excluded from `clinical_any` pending measurement. | T033 Finding |

**Validated against:** **i2b2/VA 2010 concept extraction** → `problem`; **ShARe/CLEF eHealth 2013-2014** → `disorder`; **SNOMED CT Entity Linking Challenge** → `clinical finding`

Sheet: [`disorder_NER_validation.md`](../validation/pipeline/categories/disorder_NER_validation.md)

### `lab_measurement` — Laboratory measurements, either convention

A laboratory analyte named in a note, whichever way the naming is read. Deliberately spans both readings of `Hgb-9.9`, because UMLS and the SNOMED challenge annotators disagree about which one it is and both are defensible: UMLS types `hgb` as T034, a test *result*, while the annotators chose a T059 concept, the *procedure* that produces it. The divergence accounts for roughly 640 abbreviation-shaped gold spans and the largest single bucket of monosemous-but-wrong matches. Neither reading is corrected, because neither is wrong. This category is how a user says "the analyte, however it is typed" without having to know which convention their corpus was annotated under.

| Category | Tier | Definition | Semantic types |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lab_measurement` | `anchored` | _(above)_ | T034 Laboratory or Test Result, T059 Laboratory Procedure |

**Validated against:** **SNOMED CT Entity Linking Challenge** → `gold spans whose concept carries T034 or T059 — both are annotated, and the disagreement is about which, not whether
`

Sheet: [`lab_measurement_NER_validation.md`](../validation/pipeline/categories/lab_measurement_NER_validation.md)

### `lab_result` — Laboratory and test results

The outcome of a test rather than the test itself — the value or its qualitative reading. Numeric values are handled by the numeric extractors; this covers the named result concepts.

| Category | Tier | Definition | Semantic types |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lab_result` | `unanchored` | _(above)_ | T034 Laboratory or Test Result |

**Validated against:** _no gold standard covers this._

Sheet: [`lab_result_NER_validation.md`](../validation/pipeline/categories/lab_result_NER_validation.md)

### `medication` — Medications

Drugs and pharmacologic substances the patient is given. Deliberately tight — T121 Pharmacologic Substance, T200 Clinical Drug and T195 Antibiotic only. Widening it to the broader chemical types admitted every amino acid in the terminology and clinical abbreviations that collide with element symbols.

| Category | Tier | Definition | Semantic types |
|---|---|---|---|
| `medication` | `anchored` | _(above)_ | T121 Pharmacologic Substance, T195 Antibiotic, T200 Clinical Drug |

**Validated against:** **i2b2/VA 2010 concept extraction** → `treatment (partial)`; **n2c2 2018 Track 2 (medication and ADE)** → `drug`

Sheet: [`medication_NER_validation.md`](../validation/pipeline/categories/medication_NER_validation.md)

### `procedure` — Procedures

Things done to or for the patient — operations, therapies, imaging, lab work and other health-care activities. Split into therapeutic and diagnostic because "the treatment was corrupted" and "the test was corrupted" are different experiments.

| Category | Tier | Definition | Semantic types |
|---|---|---|---|
| `procedure` | `anchored` | _(above)_ | T058 Health Care Activity, T059 Laboratory Procedure, T060 Diagnostic Procedure, T061 Therapeutic or Preventive Procedure, T062 Research Activity, T063 Molecular Biology Research Technique, T065 Educational Activity |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;↳ `therapeutic_procedure` | `derived` | Interventions intended to treat or prevent — surgery, dialysis, transfusion, physiotherapy. Evidence of treatment, which many phenotype definitions use as a proxy for the condition treated. | T061 Therapeutic or Preventive Procedure |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;↳ `diagnostic_procedure` | `derived` | Tests and investigations performed to establish a diagnosis — imaging, laboratory procedures, biopsies. The procedure, not its result. | T059 Laboratory Procedure, T060 Diagnostic Procedure |

**Validated against:** **i2b2/VA 2010 concept extraction** → `test + treatment (partial — i2b2 treatment also covers drugs)`; **SNOMED CT Entity Linking Challenge** → `procedure`

Sheet: [`procedure_NER_validation.md`](../validation/pipeline/categories/procedure_NER_validation.md)

## Prevalence in the development corpus

200 MIMIC-IV discharge summaries. Word-level lookup, so these are
**upper bounds** — see [validation/protocol.md](../validation/protocol.md).

The rows overlap and do not sum to 100%: a parent counts everything its
children do, and a word may carry several semantic types. For shares
that sum, use the primary category below.

| Category | % of content tokens | Distinct word types |
|---|---|---|
| `disorder` | 21.1% | 1,940 |
| `procedure` | 11.7% | 935 |
| `finding` | 10.3% | 834 |
| `anatomy` | 10.1% | 712 |
| `medication` | 9.3% | 1,176 |
| `disease` | 8.1% | 1,061 |
| `symptom` | 4.4% | 226 |
| `diagnostic_procedure` | 4.3% | 358 |
| `therapeutic_procedure` | 3.2% | 437 |
| `device` | 1.6% | 219 |
| `lab_result` | 0.9% | 25 |

## Categories overlap; a table needs one per word

The categories above are sets of semantic types, and they overlap by
design: `finding` and `symptom` lie inside `disorder`, `lab_measurement`
shares types with `lab_result` and `procedure`, and one concept can carry
several types. `robustehr.categories.categories_of` returns every category
that admits a concept, which is what a target needs (`cat=medication`
means any concept that is a medication).

A table whose rows must sum needs exactly one category per word.
`robustehr.categories.primary_category` gives it: the first category in
this order that admits the concept.

`disease` > `finding` > `symptom` > `medication` > `anatomy` > `procedure` > `lab_result` > `device`

Two outcomes are not categories and are returned as themselves:
`uncategorized` when a concept matched and none of its types is in the
order, and `no_concept` when no concept covers the word (pass `None`).
`finding` precedes `symptom` because the published tables were computed
that way; the two share a display group, so the choice shows only when
they are read separately. The order is declared under `exclusive_order`
in `semantic_categories.yaml`.

For reading, the primary categories are grouped
(`robustehr.categories.display_groups`):

| Display group | Primary categories |
|---|---|
| Diseases and diagnoses | `disease` |
| Signs, symptoms and findings | `finding`, `symptom` |
| Procedures and tests | `procedure`, `lab_result` |
| Medications | `medication` |
| Anatomy | `anatomy` |
| Other | `device`, `uncategorized`, `no_concept` |

## Removed categories

Cut for irrelevance to clinical notes rather than for being
indefensible, each measured on the same 200 notes first:

| Category | Measured | Why removed |
|---|---|---|
| `chemical` | 11.1% of tokens | Matches were abbreviation collisions (`sig`, `bid`, `date`), not clinical substance. Drugs are covered by `medication`; the rest is research chemistry. |
| `organism` | 1.7%, 149 of 99,788 terms used | Top matches `patient`, `major`, `areas`. Pathogens matter but need concept-level matching, not a 100,000-term word list. |
| `physiology` | 6.1% of tokens | Overlapped `disorder` and `finding`, with `pain`, `status`, `instructions` on top. Vital signs are handled by the numeric extractors. |
